answer: Because the vault forfeiture is applied at exit, the sonnet ledger totals each burn, and the horizon audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 195 aliases therefore destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 40% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned and therefore nobody profits from it. That is 40 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
